pedagogy.summary: This topic has two linked strands: automatic recall of addition and subtraction facts to 20 (so 7+8 and 15−8 come without calculating) and derivation of related facts to 100 by scaling and using known bonds (6+4=10 → 60+40=100; 5+5=10 → 35+5=40). Recall is built from secure make-ten strategy plus spaced retrieval, not speed drills; derivation is built by treating tens as units, so a known bond reappears at a larger scale.
bestPractices: Build automaticity from strategy, then retrieval: secure make-ten within 20 first, then space low-stakes recall practice so facts move to memory (DfE: emphasis on practice aids fluency)
Teach fact families so + and − are learned together (7+8=15, 15−8=7, 15−7=8) and the inverse is available
Derive decade facts by scaling a known bond: 6+4=10 becomes 60+40=100 because six tens plus four tens is ten tens
Use the same visual at two scales (ten-frame counters vs ten-rods) to show 6+4 and 60+40 are one picture
Avoid timed pressure that induces anxiety; keep finger/strategy use welcome while retrieval matures
keyRepresentations: Fact-family triangle (shows the three related facts)
Base-ten ten-rods (scaling a bond to tens)
commonMisconceptions: Recall not automatic — still counting on fingers every time for 7+8
Failing to scale the bond: knowing 6+4=10 but giving 60+40=10 or 70 or 700
Treating addition and subtraction as unrelated, so 15−8 is re-counted despite knowing 7+8=15
Applying a derived pattern blindly (e.g. 35+5=40 but then 35+50=40)

learn.summary: Two linked goals for ages 6–7: automatic recall of addition and subtraction facts to 20 (so 7+8 and 15−8 come without calculating) and derivation of related facts to 100 by scaling and using known bonds — 6+4=10 → 60+40=100 by scaling the bond to tens, and 5+5=10 → 35+5=40 by using the ones bond inside a larger number. Recall is built from a secure make-ten strategy plus spaced, untimed retrieval rather than speed drills; derivation is built by treating tens as units so a known bond reappears at a larger scale.

activities.title: Same bond, bigger units: scaling 6+4 to 60+40
feedback: If a child gives 60+40=10, 70 or 700, show 6+4 and 60+40 with the same picture at two scales (counters then ten-rods) and name that six tens plus four tens is ten tens = 100.
If a child says 35+50=40, slow down and count the tens being added: adding five tens to 35 gives 85, while adding five ones gives 40. Keep both comparisons visible side by side.
When a child derives correctly, ask 'how did you know that?' so the scaling or ones-bond reasoning is spoken, not just the answer.
activities.rationale: Using the same visual at two scales makes 'derive' concrete: a known within-ten bond is reused at the scale of tens by unitising. A manipulable or scalable model lets the learner see the identical make-ten action produce 10 and then 100; a fixed two-scale picture can also show this relationship.
sourceClaims: Year 2 pupils recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently and derive and use related facts up to 100 (e.g. 3+7=10 → 30+70=100); an emphasis on practice at this stage aids fluency, and knowing number bonds establishes addition and subtraction as related operations.
Recall of pairs that make ten supports calculation, and known facts are extended by unitising tens so a within-ten bond is reused at the scale of tens.
learnerActions: Complete 6+4 on a ten-frame by sliding four counters in to fill all ten; confirm this is a known, secure bond making 10.
Switch the counters to tens: let each counter become a ten-rod (or restate each counter as 'one ten') so the same full frame now reads 100.
Say aloud what changed: 'six tens plus four tens is ten tens, which is 100' — the gesture and picture are identical, only the unit changed.
Repeat the tens-scaling with another known bond: 5+5=10 → 50+50=100 (five tens plus five tens is ten tens).
Separately, derive 35+5 by using the ones bond 5+5=10: 30 + (5+5) = 40, so here the 5 is added as five ones, not scaled to tens.
Deliberately contrast 35+5=40 with 35+50=85: in 35+50 you are adding five tens, not five ones, so the answers differ.
activities.intendedInsight: Deriving a decade fact like 60+40 is scaling a known bond, not memorising a new fact: six tens plus four tens is ten tens = 100. A different move is using a bond inside a larger number — 35+5 uses the ones bond 5+5=10 to give 40. Which unit you add (ones vs tens) decides the result, so 35+5=40 and 35+50=85 are different.

activities.title: Fact-family triangle: one trio, both operations
feedback: If a child re-counts 15−8 straight after giving 7+8=15, lay out the fact family 7, 8, 15 and show the same three numbers make both facts.
Prompt: 'If 7+8=15, what subtraction facts do you already know without working them out?'
A tap-to-reveal triangle is good reference for the inverse link but does not by itself build recall speed; pair it with retrieval practice.
activities.rationale: Teaching fact families makes the inverse explicit so + and − are learned together and the inverse is immediately available. This supports the misconception where subtraction is treated as a separate unknown fact.
sourceClaims: Year 2 pupils recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently and derive and use related facts up to 100 (e.g. 3+7=10 → 30+70=100); an emphasis on practice at this stage aids fluency, and knowing number bonds establishes addition and subtraction as related operations.
learnerActions: Lay out the three numbers 7, 8 and 15 on a fact-family triangle (part–part–whole).
Cover one corner and read off the fact it reveals: cover 15 to get 7+8=15 and 8+7=15; cover 7 to get 15−8=7; cover 8 to get 15−7=8.
State explicitly: because 7+8=15, you already know 15−8 and 15−7 without re-counting.
Build a second family (e.g. 6, 9, 15, giving 6+9=15, 9+6=15, 15−6=9, 15−9=6) and name all its related facts the same way.
activities.intendedInsight: Addition and subtraction are the same relationship between three numbers; knowing one fact hands you the inverse, so 15−8 need not be re-counted once 7+8=15 is known.

activities.title: Spaced, untimed retrieval to build automatic recall
feedback: If a child counts on fingers for 7+8 every time with no drop in effort on a second asking, do NOT impose timed drills or penalise finger use — keep practising the make-ten strategy and spaced recall without the clock.
For a derive prompt like '6+4=10, so 60+40=?', if a wrong value such as 10, 70 or 700 is chosen, return to the two-scale picture and re-establish six tens plus four tens = 100.
Ask 'which of those did you just know, and which did you have to work out?' to make the recall/calculation distinction visible to the learner.
activities.rationale: Recall is built from a secure make-ten strategy then moved to memory by spaced low-stakes practice; timed pressure can induce anxiety and is avoided. A self-paced fill-in or choice format can exercise retrieval and check the derive insight, but repeated spaced practice, not a single check, is what builds automaticity.
sourceClaims: Year 2 pupils recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently and derive and use related facts up to 100 (e.g. 3+7=10 → 30+70=100); an emphasis on practice at this stage aids fluency, and knowing number bonds establishes addition and subtraction as related operations.
Recall of pairs that make ten supports calculation, and known facts are extended by unitising tens so a within-ten bond is reused at the scale of tens.
learnerActions: Practise recalling facts to 20 in short, low-stakes sessions spread over days (e.g. 7+8, 15−8, 6+4, 9+4), rather than one long timed drill.
Mix in derive-a-fact prompts such as '6+4=10, so 60+40=?' and '5+5=10, so 35+5=?', choosing or writing the answer.
After each prompt, say which ones you just knew and which you had to work out.
Keep finger and make-ten strategy use welcome; the aim is that repeated facts need less effort each time, not beating a clock.
activities.intendedInsight: Automaticity grows from secure strategy plus spaced, untimed retrieval; a fact becomes 'known' when recalling it needs noticeably less effort on later encounters.

activities.title: Playful recall talk: 'how did you know that?'
feedback: Spoken back-and-forth gives retrieval practice but does not by itself build the make-ten strategy or the scaling insight; pair it with the ten-frame and two-scale work.
If a child cannot explain how they knew a fact, return to the relevant model (ten-frame or fact-family triangle) before more recall practice.
activities.rationale: A conversational recall routine offers extra retrieval opportunities and surfaces thinking, complementing the manipulative and the fact-family work without replacing the strategy-building they provide.
learnerActions: Trade quick spoken recall prompts back and forth with a partner or adult (flashcard-style), e.g. one asks 7+8, then 15−8, then 6+4.
For each answer, the asker follows up with 'how did you know that?' — did you just know it, make ten, or use the inverse?
Keep it low-stakes and untimed; celebrate strategy explanations as much as correct answers.
activities.intendedInsight: Verbalising recall and the reasoning behind it reinforces both the facts and the strategies (make-ten, inverse, scaling) that generate them.

constraints: Do not use timed drills or penalise finger/strategy use; automaticity is to grow from a secure make-ten strategy plus spaced, untimed retrieval.

A tap-to-reveal fact-family triangle is a reference scaffold for the inverse relationship; it does not exercise retrieval speed or the scaling derivation, so pair it with practice and the two-scale model.
A fill-in or choice retrieval format can check the derive insight and give recall practice, but a single check does not build automaticity; genuine fluency needs repeated spaced practice over time.
Recognition/choice responses alone do not elicit independent construction of a derived fact; include prompts where the child states or writes the answer and explains the scaling.
A conversational recall routine is a supplementary retrieval vehicle; it does not directly build the make-ten strategy or the scaling insight.

Keep the ones-vs-tens distinction explicit (35+5=40 by adding five ones vs 35+50=85 by adding five tens) so the derived pattern is not applied blindly, and keep scaling to tens (60+40) distinct from using a ones bond inside a number (35+5).
reviewNotes: This is an agent semantic rewrite of saved teaching research without fresh source verification; sources were not re-fetched, and activities are research-informed proposals, not validated interventions.

Self-audit arithmetic check: 6+4=10 and 60+40=100 (six tens + four tens = ten tens) are correct; 5+5=10, 50+50=100, 35+5=40 are correct; 35+50=85 is correct. The original source field left 35+50 only as a 'why not same answer?' probe without stating the value; the correct value 85 has been added so the contrast is taught, not left ambiguous.

Scaling (60+40, 50+50) and using a ones bond inside a larger number (35+5) are kept as two distinct derivation types; the summary and intendedInsight were adjusted so 35+5 is not mislabelled as a scaling case.

The legacy claim that '3D adds nothing' and that number facts 'are not spatial' is a catalog preference, not an established pedagogical law; it has been dropped rather than asserted. Ten-frames and base-ten rods are themselves spatial supports for these facts.

The legacy framing that a scalable tool 'turns derive into it's the same fact' overstates necessity; a fixed two-scale picture can also show the relationship, so the activity keeps the model affordance without claiming one medium is uniquely required.
The original bead string / Rekenrek representation was not carried into these activities; it remains a valid make-ten manipulative if an implementer wishes to add it.

probeDeeper: You knew 6 + 4 = 10 — how does that help you with 60 + 40?
If 7 + 8 = 15, what subtraction facts do you already know without working them out?
You said 35 + 5 = 40. What about 35 + 50 — same answer? Why not?
Which of those did you just know, and which did you have to work out?
assess.correctAnswer: 15, 7, 10, 100, 40. Fluent: 7+8 and 15−8 recalled (or via make-ten) without counting; 60+40 derived by scaling 6+4 (six tens + four tens = ten tens = 100); 35+5 derived from 5+5=10 → 40.

errorPatterns.pattern: Recall not yet automatic — counts on fingers for 7+8 and 15−8 every time, no faster on a second asking
errorPatterns.nextMove: Do NOT impose timed drills or penalise finger use — automaticity grows from spaced, low-stakes retrieval built on a secure make-ten strategy, not speed pressure. Keep practising strategy and recall without the clock.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: Correct answers but visible counting each time; no drop in effort when the same fact recurs

errorPatterns.pattern: Fails to scale the bond — 'six and four is ten, so sixty and forty is ten' (or 70, or 700)
errorPatterns.nextMove: Show 6+4 and 60+40 with the same picture at two scales (counters then ten-rods); name that six tens plus four tens is ten tens, which is 100.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: For 60+40 the answer ignores that each number is a group of tens; the bond isn't reused at the ten-scale

errorPatterns.pattern: Inverse not linked — answers 7+8=15 instantly but re-counts 15−8 as if it were a separate, unknown fact
errorPatterns.nextMove: Lay out the fact family 7, 8, 15 and show the same three numbers make both facts, so knowing one hands you the other.
errorPatterns.revealedBy: No drop in effort on 15−8 despite having just given 7+8=15

responseLevels.gap: Counts out every fact including 7+8; gives 60+40 as 10 or 70; treats + and − as unrelated.
responseLevels.full: Instant recall of facts to 20 and their inverses, derives 60+40=100 and 35+5=40 by scaling and using known bonds, and explains the link.
responseLevels.partial: Recalls within-20 facts but cannot yet derive the scaled facts, or derives 60+40 only with prompting; the inverse link is emerging.

assess.diagnosticPrompt: Rapid-fire, watching for hesitation and finger-counting: ask 7 + 8, then 15 − 8, then 6 + 4; then 'use 6 + 4 to tell me 60 + 40', then 'what's 35 + 5?'. Note which come instantly and which are counted out.
assess.whatMakesItDiscriminate: Speed and effort on 7+8 and 15−8 separate recall from calculation. 60+40 separates a child who scales the known bond from one who says 10 or 700. 15−8 separates a child who uses the inverse of 7+8 from one who re-counts despite just answering 7+8.
